adds.title: LGBT rights in Brazil (Wikipedia) - LGBTQ people in Brazilian prisons
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBT rights in Brazil' (fetched and read in full, 4 Oct 2026) states, in its Politics section, that LGBTQ people have a special place in Brazilian prisons, separate from other prisoners; that transsexuals have the right to be called by their social name and not their birth name and to be forwarded to women's prisons; and that LGBTQ people in prisons may choose male or female clothing. The sentence is footnoted to G1's 17 Apr 2014 report ('Governo publica portaria com direitos para presos gays e travestis', archived 12 Jul 2018) - i.e., the cited legal grounding is a 2014 federal portaria granting rights to gay and travesti prisoners. Placement axis: on paper, placement follows gender identity (trans prisoners forwarded to women's prisons), with separate custody for LGBTQ prisoners, social-name use and clothing choice; the underlying citation is dated (2014) and its current status was not independently re-verified.

adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia) - Brazil section
adds.summary: Wikipedia overview article (fetched and read in full, 4 Oct 2026). Its Transgender issues > Brazil section contains no trans-prisoner placement rule - only discussion of social vulnerability, stigma and fragmented identity of travestis and transgender people during rehabilitation; international sections show placement norms elsewhere (e.g., Canada placing by gender identity, Italy's admission discretion). Negative evidence: this general overview documents no Brazil-specific trans-prisoner housing policy, special unit or segregation-for-placement practice.

records.note: no Goias-specific prison-placement data found. Wikipedia full-text search 'transgender prisoner Goias prison' (MediaWiki API) returned no jurisdiction-specific article - only generic hits (LGBTQ rights in Brazil, Human rights in Brazil; Goias mentions unrelated to trans-prisoner placement). The operative national signal, documented by Wikipedia's Brazil coverage and footnoted to a G1 report of 17 Apr 2014 on a federal portaria for gay and travesti prisoners: transgender prisoners have the right to be called by their social name and not their birth name and to be forwarded to women's prisons; LGBTQ prisoners have a special place in Brazilian prisons, separate from other prisoners, and may choose male or female clothing - i.e., placement follows gender identity on paper. No Goias state policy, special custody unit, or court ruling on trans-prisoner placement was located within budget; the citation is from 2014, so current status should be flagged for verification.
